note: Sailors slept in hammocks slung from beams below deck.
Demeanour: the way a person behaves and carries himself.
Ascendancy: a position of influence and power over others.

anchor: Captain the Honorable Edward Fairfax Vere
note: “The Honorable” is a courtesy title for the younger son of a lord, showing that Vere is of noble birth.
Prolific: producing abundantly. The age produced many famous sailors.
Allied: related by family. Vere has high-ranking relatives.
Infraction: a breaking of a rule.

anchor: intrepid to the verge of temerity
note: Intrepid: fearless. Temerity: reckless boldness.
Injudiciously: without good judgment. Vere is bold but never rash.

anchor: Flag-Lieutenant under Rodney in that Admiral’s crowning victory over De Grasse
note: In April 1782 Admiral Rodney defeated the French admiral de Grasse in the West Indies and took him prisoner. A flag-lieutenant is the admiral’s personal aide.
source: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th ed. (1911), “Grasse, François Joseph Paul, Comte de”, https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Grasse%2C_Fran%C3%A7ois_Joseph_Paul%2C_Comte_de

note: A post-captain held the full rank of captain and commanded a large ship, as opposed to a commander.
source: W. H. Smyth, The Sailor’s Word-Book (1867), “Post-captain”, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/26000

anchor: never garnished unprofessional talk with nautical terms
note: Garnished: decorated. Vere avoided sprinkling sailors’ slang into ordinary talk.
Paramount: highest in importance, here demanding his full action.
Undemonstrative: not showing feelings openly.

anchor: the silent deference of the officers retiring to leeward
note: Deference: respectful courtesy. Officers kept to the leeward side, away from the wind, leaving the windward side to the captain.
Envoy: a messenger or diplomat sent abroad.
Unobtrusiveness: not drawing attention to himself.

anchor: a certain unaffected modesty of manhood
note: Unaffected: natural, without pretense. His modesty is real.
Vere falls into reveries, gazing at the empty sea.
Irascibility: a tendency to flare up in anger.
Appellation: a name or title.
Andrew Marvell (1621 to 1678) was an English poet. He lived at the Fairfax estate and wrote a poem on it.
Appleton House is a poem by Marvell about the Yorkshire home of Lord Fairfax, where Marvell was a tutor in 1650.

anchor: a hero in the German wars of the seventeenth century
note: Melville gives Vere’s family an ancestor who was a soldier abroad in the Thirty Years’ War.
Severe: strict and hard, as the family’s discipline was.

anchor: brimming over with just family pride
note: Just: deserved. His pride in his cousin is well earned.
Currency: general acceptance. The nickname spread.
Novel: new. Prefix: here, “Starry,” placed before the surname.
